content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"This judge text compares the challenger's and defender's chains by footing in a chain-against-chain collision, which is what rule K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"never verse by verse: I weighed whether the judge's lack-of-naming reason is a forbidden word-for-word stating-verse test or a permissible chain-footing observation.","why":"The judge calls the result underdetermined partly because the challenger's chain does not name Joseph as the begetter, which uses the retired stating-verse/word-for-word test rather than weighing support by footing as K-C requires."}
